notes.levels: A snapshot's level for a signal is 0 below a band's `from`, then `base` at `from` rising linearly (by `slope`) to base + slope at `to`. The window's level is the larger of its mean (sustained trouble) and `spike_share` of its worst (a spike counts, but a single one stays minor). A level under `min` isn't reported; from `major` an issue is major, from `critical` critical.
notes.severity_cap: The best score an issue of each severity allows: any issue rules out an A, a major one a B, a critical one a C.
notes.bands: A band is the first value that counts (`from`) and the value that is as bad as it gets (`to`), set for a wired or good Wi-Fi LAN, the product's target. fps_ratio runs downward (shown over sent: under 95% is visible stutter, under 60% a slideshow). dropped, skipped: per second as a share of the target rate. decode_budget: decode time over the frame budget (1000 / fps). latency: p50 in ms, under 20 is an A on a LAN. delivery_spread: delivery p95 over p50, ms. latency_spread: the interquartile range of the latency across the window, ms. jitter_buffer: WebRTC wait per frame, ms. lost_frames: WebTransport frames FEC couldn't rebuild, per second. lost_packets: WebRTC packets per second (it retransmits). recovered, partial: frames per second. rtt: ms. node_*, streamer_cpu: percent; the streamer's CPU is a share of the whole machine, or of one core when the core count is unknown. audio_jitter_wt: our own buffer, which sits at 0 on a calm LAN. audio_jitter_rtc: the browser's NetEq, which holds 30-60 ms on a perfect LAN in Chrome and Safari.
notes.params: busy_sent_fps: the streamer sends only when the picture changes, so stutter, decoding and freezes are judged only while it sends at least this many frames per second (not at all without a send rate). gpu_late_encode: the node's GPU load counts only while the streamer's composited to encoded p99 is past this share of the frame budget. freeze_*: the longest wait between frames must beat max(freeze_min_ms, freeze_budgets frame budgets, freeze_budgets send intervals) to count, and freeze_to_ms is as bad as it gets; with no gap measure, a second with no frames is a gap of no_frames_gap_ms. latency_spread_samples: fewest latencies the spread needs. sound_*: decoded sound counts as sound above sound_present (peak, 0..1), the output plays nothing under sound_played, and sound_out_seconds of that report it. The sound levels are first + step per further occurrence (or second).

issues.title: Stuttering picture
issues.hint: Frames are being sent but not all of them show. Check the other lines: if the network is fine, try 60 fps or another codec; if it isn't, a cable beats Wi-Fi.

hint.web: The browser decoded frames it had no time to show. Close heavy tabs and apps on this computer, or try 60 fps.
hint.native: The player decoded frames it had no time to show. Close heavy apps on this Mac, or try 60 fps.

hint.web: Your browser or computer can't decode fast enough. Try 60 fps or another codec (HEVC and H.264 are hardware-decoded on most machines), and close other heavy apps.
hint.native: This Mac can't decode fast enough. Try 60 fps or another codec (HEVC and H.264 are hardware-decoded), and close other heavy apps.

details.main: {decode:ms1} to decode a frame, of {budget:ms1} per frame

issues.title: Picture freezes
issues.hint: No frames arrived for a moment while the node was sending. Usually a network stall (Wi-Fi roaming or interference, a busy link) or a node that stopped to catch up; a cable is the first thing to try.

hint.web: Frames take long from the node to your screen. Check the network (a cable, not Wi-Fi) and whether the node is busy; a lower frame rate or bitrate can help on a weak link.
hint.native: Frames take long from arriving here to showing. This Mac is busy or the decoder is falling behind; close other apps, or lower the frame rate or bitrate.

issues.title: Uneven latency
issues.hint: Delivery time varies from frame to frame, which shows as judder. Queueing on the network (other traffic, Wi-Fi) is the usual cause.

details.latency: latency wanders by {spread:ms0} over the last seconds

issues.title: Packet loss
issues.hint: The network is dropping packets, which costs frames or forces resends. Wi-Fi interference or a congested link: try a cable, or move closer to the access point.

issues.title: Network needs repair
issues.hint: Error correction is rebuilding frames that lost packets, so you see nothing yet, but the link is dropping data and a worse moment would show. Wi-Fi or a busy link: try a cable.

issues.title: Frames skipped
issues.hint: PyroWave frames that lost a packet and were overtaken by the next whole one are skipped: each costs one frame, and the next shows whole. Many of them read as stutter. The link is dropping data, often because it is nearly full: 4:2:0 or 60 fps leaves room, and a cable beats Wi-Fi.

issues.title: Frames shown incomplete
issues.hint: PyroWave shows a frame from the packets that arrived, so a lost packet softens a few blocks for one frame instead of breaking the picture. The link is dropping data, often because it is nearly full: 4:2:0 or 60 fps leaves room, and a cable beats Wi-Fi.

issues.title: Slow network round trip
issues.hint: The round trip to the node is long for a LAN. Check you are on the same network as the node, and for a VPN or Wi-Fi in the way.

issues.title: Node overloaded
issues.hint: The machine running the environment is out of something, so frames are made late. Close other apps on it, lower the frame rate, or choose another device.

issues.title: Sound restarted
issues.hint: The page's sound decoder or track failed and was rebuilt, so a few milliseconds of sound were lost instead of the rest of the session. Once in a while is harmless; if it repeats, use Restart sound, or reload the page and tell us what the browser's console says.

issues.title: Sound not reaching the speakers
issues.hint: Sound is arriving and decoding, but the browser's audio output plays none of it. Use Restart sound; if that doesn't help, check the computer's output device, and quit and reopen the browser, which has cleared this before.

details.main: sound arriving (peak {peak:f2}) but {seconds:f0} s of silence played

issues.title: Sound buffering
issues.hint: Sound packets are arriving late, so the player holds more sound back to keep it smooth, and the sound runs behind the picture; past the buffer it crackles. A busy or lossy link does this: a cable helps, and so does a lighter codec or frame rate when the link is nearly full.

issues.title: Wi-Fi latency spikes
issues.hint: Likely AWDL (AirDrop/Continuity) taking turns with Wi-Fi. A cable avoids it; see the README.

details.main: frames arrive in bursts, typical of AWDL (AirDrop, Continuity)
